first.rationale: Current situation shows dual problems: activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 (activation messaging inside product improved week-one engagement) directly targets the activation decline with proven mechanism. Memory_86 (onboarding improvements lifted adoption) supports the connection. Verification of memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_91 (activation messaging) will confirm which lever—friction reduction vs. behavioral nudging—has stronger evidence in our specific context. Activation messaging is the higher-leverage play: it works on engaged accounts already in the funnel, doesn't sacrifice pricing power against competitor pressure, and addresses the immediate 6% activation decline. Referral incentives (memory_57) work only on established customers and don't help current acquisition pressure. Promotional_pricing (memory_73) could address SMB churn but memory_91/memory_86 suggest activation/onboarding are the real constraints. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB activation problem. Standard_experiment scale preserves room for rapid iteration if needed.

mid.rationale: Verification confirms activation_messaging as the optimal single experiment for this cycle. Memory_91 showed +6% activation lift with +1% retention gain (no downside), directly addressing the 6% QoQ activation decline we face. Memory_31 (signup simplification) delivered +9% activation but incurred -1% retention risk, making it higher-friction for decision at this moment. In-product activation messaging is lower-risk: it engages existing users post-signup without increasing acquisition friction or sacrificing pricing power against competitor pressure. The +11% week-one engagement lift from memory_91 compounds with memory_86's onboarding improvements (both push toward faster time-to-value). This preserves optionality: if activation messaging succeeds, we can layer signup simplification in a subsequent cycle. If it underperforms, we retain the option to test promotional pricing or referral tactics. Standard experiment scale allows learning without overcommitting. Primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue is best served by fixing engagement leaks in the funnel before competing on price.

final2.rationale: Competitive threat has escalated materially: doubled churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB segment represent immediate revenue at risk. Promotional_pricing (memory_73) showed strong acquisition and revenue lift in SMB and is the only tested lever that directly counters price-based competitor attack. Activation_messaging remains valid long-term but is too slow against acute churn velocity. The downside risk is real: targeted promotional pricing can compress margins and may train price-sensitive cohorts toward discount dependency, creating downstream LTV erosion. However, the alternative—allowing competitor to capture our SMB base during aggressive entry phase—creates larger long-term qualified revenue damage. Memory_73 evidence is sufficient to justify standard_experiment scale on this segment with guardrails (time-limited pricing, cohort-specific application, retention monitoring). This decision trades near-term margin preservation for retention of the customer base and optionality to re-engage on value once competitive pressure normalizes. The choice preserves uncertainty about optimal long-term positioning while acting decisively on immediate existential threat to SMB revenue.
